::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[What open cover should i consider in order to show $(X,d)$ is not compact?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2058655/what-open-cover-should-i-consider-in-order-to-show-x-d-is-not-compact), asked by [Styles](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/329752/styles) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2016-12-14; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Let $X= \mathbb R$,let
>
> $d(x,y)=\frac{\left|x-y\right|}{1+\vert  x-y \vert} \forall x,y \in \mathbb R$.
>
> Show that $(X,d)$ is not compact.
>
> What is the form of open sets of $(X,d)$?
:::

If $X$ were compact, the map $f \colon X \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto d(x,0)$ would have a compact image.  Does it?
